category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: No written agreement but UPI evidence
expected: Confirms oral tenancies with electronic banking records constitute valid proof of tenancy and financial consideration.
prompt: I don't have a written rental agreement, but I have all monthly rent and deposit UPI transaction receipts. Can I claim my deposit?
raw_response:
Hello, I am LawPilot AI, your Indian legal assistant for tenancy, consumer, and employment matters.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant renting a property without a formal written rental agreement, but you possess complete UPI transaction receipts for your monthly rent payments and security deposit. The core issue is whether you can legally claim a refund of your security deposit from your landlord despite the absence of a written contract.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 108(m) and (o), a tenant is bound to restore the property in as good condition as received, subject only to reasonable wear and tear, which refers to the normal deterioration of property resulting from intended use over time without negligence or misuse.
- The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state tenancy laws) mandates that any security deposit must be refunded to the tenant upon vacating the premises, after making only valid deductions agreed upon under the tenancy arrangement.
- Even in the absence of a written rental agreement, oral tenancies are legally recognized under Indian law, and your UPI transaction receipts serve as valid primary documentary evidence of an ongoing tenancy and the payment of the security deposit.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect all your UPI transaction receipts, bank statements proving deposit transfers, and any WhatsApp chats or call logs exchanged with your landlord regarding the deposit.
2. Send written demand notice granting 15 days: Issue a formal written demand notice to your landlord via registered post or email, clearly stating the deposit amount paid through UPI, demanding its full refund within 15 days, and noting that reasonable wear and tear cannot be deducted.
3. Appropriate forum: If the landlord fails to refund the amount within 15 days, you can approach the local Rent Authority or file a summary recovery suit before the Civil Court or Consumer Commission, depending on your state jurisdiction.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is the total security deposit amount you paid, and in which city or state is the rental property located?

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Protection of tenant against eviction and restoration of essential amenities
